continuity_scope: Black Clover, Vol. 1, VIZ English digital edition (Shonen Jump imprint; 193 pages; eISBN 978-1-4215-9077-6; released 2016-06-07). This is a narrow selected-volume pass. It excludes later manga volumes, Japanese editions as independent witnesses, anime, films, games, novels, guidebooks, and other adaptations.
coverage_rule: Include individual dramatic characters directly named and described in VIZ's selected Volume 1 product copy or its official Volume 1 editorial coverage. Those sources name Asta and Yuno; both are recorded. The public Chapter 1 reader is retained as a primary manga locator, but no unquoted panel detail is added beyond the official metadata coverage.
omissions: All other Volume 1 people, whose names or claim-specific descriptions are not available in the selected official metadata evidence.
Magic Knights, squads, grimoires, magic/anti-magic, peoples, kingdoms, places, and themes as character nodes; they are dimensions or terms only.
All later manga, Japanese-edition, anime, film, game, novel, guidebook, and adaptive material.
content_cautions: VIZ labels Volume 1 Teen. Its official Volume 1 review describes a confrontation with a magic thief and a magic-negating sword; this pass does not catalogue violence or reproduce scene detail.
Asta's lack of magic is a fictional setting premise. No real-world disability, diagnosis, impairment, or class-equivalence claim is made.

The selected VIZ copy calls Asta young and the Japanese publisher portal says Asta and Yuno were raised at a church, but neither selected English product synopsis labels either an orphan; this pass does not infer orphan status.
uncertainties: VIZ's accessible Volume 1 product page does not name an English translator; no translator is inferred.

The official Volume 1 product description names Asta only. Yuno and the rivalry are included from VIZ's official Volume 1 editorial review and Shueisha's official manga portal, not from the product synopsis alone.
The selected evidence does not establish exact social class, a medical or disability framework, Magic Knight membership, squad affiliation, detailed grimoire rules, or a full anti-magic system.
Anime, game, film, novel, and other adaptation continuities are separate and unreviewed.
evidence_basis: VIZ's official English Volume 1 product record and public Chapter 1 reader identify the selected witness; VIZ's official Volume 1 editorial review supports Asta/Yuno and early premise claims. Shueisha's official manga portal corroborates the early Asta-Yuno church upbringing and childhood-rival framing without importing later-only claims. No fan wiki or Wikipedia was used.
